# Antec Neo ECO Series Wattage Options & Specifications

⚡ Quick Answer

The Antec Neo ECO series power supplies are offered in four primary wattage options: 400W, 450W, 520W, and 620W. Each model is available in standard and "C" variants, such as the Neo Eco 620C. These units feature 80 PLUS certification and provide continuous power across multiple rails to ensure system stability.

...

## Available Wattage Models

The series includes both standard models and "C" variants (e.g., 400 and 400C), which share the same core power ratings and safety features but may differ in specific connector quantities. The primary wattage tiers are:

- 400 Watts: Designed for entry-level systems and office PCs.
- 450 Watts: Suitable for mid-range builds with moderate power requirements.
- 520 Watts: Targeted at performance-oriented systems with dedicated graphics cards.
- 620 Watts: The high-end option for enthusiasts and gaming rigs requiring significant power overhead.

## Power Output and Rail Specifications

Each wattage model distributes power across separate rails to maintain stability. The +12V rail is particularly critical for modern CPUs and GPUs. The maximum load capacity for each model is as follows:

### Neo Eco 400 / 400C

- +3.3V: 20A
- +5V: 20A
- +12V: 30A
- -12V: 0.8A
- +5VSB: 2.5A

### Neo Eco 450 / 450C

- +3.3V: 20A
- +5V: 20A
- +12V: 34A
- -12V: 0.8A
- +5VSB: 2.5A

### Neo Eco 520 / 520C

- +3.3V: 24A
- +5V: 24A
- +12V: 40A
- -12V: 0.8A
- +5VSB: 2.5A

### Neo Eco 620 / 620C

- +3.3V: 24A
- +5V: 24A
- +12V: 48A
- -12V: 0.8A
- +5VSB: 2.5A

## Wattage-Dependent Connectivity

The available power connectors scale with the wattage of the unit to accommodate the hardware typically used with those power levels. Specifically, the PCI-E configurations change based on the model:

- 400W and 450W Models: These units are equipped with a single PCI-E 6-pin connector.
- 520W and 620W Models: These higher-wattage units feature a PCI-E 6-pin plus an 8(6+2)-pin connector to support more powerful graphics cards.

Standard across all models is the 24(20+4)-pin main connector and the 8(4+4)-pin ATX12V/EPS12V CPU connector. The number of Molex and Serial ATA (SATA) connectors also increases on the 520W and 620W models to support more storage drives and accessories.

## Installation and Compatibility

Regardless of the chosen wattage, all Neo ECO units feature Universal Input, which automatically senses AC power sources between 100V and 240V. This eliminates the need for a manual voltage switch.

Note: To reduce environmental waste, a power cord is not included with the Neo ECO series. Users should reuse their existing power cord or purchase a standard high-quality cable separately. Ensure the power supply is switched to the "|" position after connecting the AC cord to the inlet.

# Antec Neo ECO Included Cables and Connectors

To identify included cables on Antec Neo ECO models, review the internal connector list. Every unit includes a 24(20+4)-pin main connector and 8(4+4)-pin ATX12V/EPS12V. Depending on the wattage, it features SATA, Molex, and PCI-E connectors. Note that an AC power cord is not included; you must reuse a standard existing cord.

...

The Antec Neo ECO series power supplies are designed to provide continuous power to your system components using a fixed set of internal cables. This series is compatible with ATX12V v2.3 and EPS12V v2.91 standards, ensuring support for modern motherboards and hardware configurations.

## Included Internal Cables

Each unit in the Neo ECO series comes equipped with a specific set of tethered cables. These connectors provide power to the motherboard, CPU, graphics card, and peripheral storage devices. The exact quantity of certain connectors varies based on the wattage and the specific model (Standard vs. C-series).

- Main Motherboard Power: A 24(20+4)-pin main connector is included for primary system power. For older motherboards requiring only 20 pins, the 4-pin section is detachable.
- CPU Power: An 8(4+4)-pin ATX12V/EPS12V connector provides dedicated power to the processor.
- Graphics Card Power: PCI-E 6-pin or 8(6+2)-pin connectors are provided. Lower wattage models (400W/450W) typically feature standard 6-pin connectors, while higher wattage models (520W/620W) include a combination of 6-pin and 8(6+2)-pin connectors.
- Storage and Accessories: Standard SATA and Molex connectors are provided for hard drives, SSDs, and optical drives. A Floppy (FDD) connector is also included for legacy hardware.

## Exclusions and Compatibility

A critical detail regarding the Neo ECO series is the exclusion of the external AC power cord. This decision is intended to reduce environmental waste by encouraging users to reuse a standard power cord from a previous build or power supply.

When connecting peripherals, you can distinguish between connector types by the wire colors. Molex connectors utilize two black wires, one yellow, and one red. SATA connectors include an additional orange power wire. If your motherboard uses a 20-pin power slot, simply detach the 4-pin attachment from the 24(20+4)-pin main connector. Do not attempt to use this detachable 4-pin section as a substitute for a dedicated 4-pin CPU (+12V) connector.

Before completing installation, ensure the AC power cord you provide is firmly connected to the AC inlet on the rear of the unit and that the power switch is toggled to the "|" (ON) position.
